tagline: Three sisters, one cauldron, and the kids get first helpings.
about: Two Salem teenagers accidentally bring the Sanderson sisters back on Halloween night and have until sunrise to stop them.

    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersBook's one-eyed devilled eggsHard-boiled eggs filled with creamy mustard yolk, each with a black olive eye and a dusting of smoked paprikaHow to make it6 eggs3 tbsp mayonnaise1 tsp Dijon mustardsalt and pepper, to taste6 pitted black olives, halved1/2 tsp smoked paprika1 tbsp chives, finely choppedLower the eggs into a pan of boiling water and boil for 10 minutes.Cool in a bowl of iced water, then peel and halve lengthways.Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise and mustard and season with salt and pepper.Spoon or pipe the filling back into the whites.Press an olive half into the middle of each egg for an eye, dust with paprika and scatter with chives.Salem town square corn dogsFrankfurts on sticks dipped in sweet polenta batter and fried golden, with tomato sauce and yellow mustardHow to make it8 frankfurts8 bamboo skewers150g fine polenta150g plain flour2 tbsp caster sugar2 tsp baking powder1/2 tsp salt1 egg250ml milk1.5 L vegetable oil, for frying125ml tomato sauce4 tbsp yellow mustardWhisk the polenta, flour, sugar, baking powder and salt, then whisk in the egg and milk to a thick batter. Pour into a tall glass.Heat the oil in a deep heavy pan to 180°C.Pat the frankfurts dry and push a skewer into each.Dip each one in the batter to coat and fry 2 or 3 at a time, turning, until deep golden, about 3 minutes.Drain on paper towel and serve hot with the tomato sauce and mustard.Baked brie with apple and honeyGilbert's shop special. Black Flame candles half off.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsWinifred's cauldron beef and pumpkin stew with herb dumplingsSlow-simmered beef with carrots and butternut pumpkin in a thick thyme gravy, with fluffy parsley dumplings steamed on topHow to make it1kg beef chuck, in 4cm cubes2 tbsp plain floursalt and pepper, to taste2 tbsp vegetable oil1 brown onion, chopped2 garlic cloves, crushed2 carrots, in chunks2 tbsp tomato paste1 L beef stock2 bay leaves1 tsp dried thyme600g butternut pumpkin, in 3cm chunks200g self-raising flour60g cold butter, diced2 tbsp parsley, chopped150ml milkToss the beef in the plain flour with salt and pepper and brown well in batches in the oil in a heavy pot. Lift out.Cook the onion, garlic and carrots in the same pot until soft.Stir in the tomato paste, then the stock, bay leaves and thyme. Return the beef, cover and simmer gently until tender.Add the pumpkin and simmer, uncovered, until just soft.Meanwhile rub the butter into the self-raising flour with the parsley and a pinch of salt, stir in the milk to a soft dough and roll into 8 balls.Sit the dumplings on top of the stew, cover and simmer until puffed and cooked through.Season the stew and ladle into bowls with 2 dumplings each.Becca's birthday pumpkin and sage mac and cheeseBecca's sixteenth, the night the Black Flame Candle gets litHow to make it600g pumpkin, diced400g macaroni40g butter40g plain flour600ml milk200g vintage cheddar, grated1 bunch sage60g panko breadcrumbs2 tbsp olive oilHeat the oven to 200°C. Roast the pumpkin in half the oil until soft, then mash.Boil the macaroni until just short of done and drain.Melt the butter, stir in the flour, whisk in the milk until thick, then add the pumpkin and most of the cheddar.Fold in the pasta, tip into a dish and top with the rest of the cheddar, crumbs and sage leaves tossed in the last of the oil. Bake until golden.SweetsBlack Flame chocolate lava puddingsDark chocolate puddings baked until just set outside with a molten middle, with vanilla ice creamHow to make it20g butter, softened, for the moulds1 tbsp cocoa powder100g dark chocolate, chopped100g butter, diced2 eggs2 egg yolks60g caster sugar2 tbsp plain flour4 scoops of vanilla ice creamBrush four 200ml pudding moulds with the soft butter and dust with the cocoa.Melt the chocolate and diced butter together in a bowl over simmering water, then cool slightly.Whisk the eggs, yolks and sugar until thick and pale.Fold in the chocolate, then the flour, and divide between the moulds.Chill until firm.Heat the oven to 200°C and bake on a tray until risen with a soft wobble in the middle.Stand for 1 minute, turn out onto plates and serve with the ice cream.DrinksSanderson green potion punchBright green kiwi, apple and lime with bruised mint, topped with lemonade and frozen grape eyeballsHow to make it4 kiwifruits, peeled500ml apple juice2 limes, 1 juiced and 1 sliced into wheels1 bunch mint12 green grapes, frozen on 4 skewers4 cups ice750ml lemonadeBlend the kiwifruit with the apple juice and lime juice until smooth.Strain into a jug through a sieve, pressing on the pulp.Bruise half the mint and stir it into the jug.Fill 4 glasses with the ice, pour in the green potion and top with the lemonade.Garnish each with a frozen grape skewer, a lime wheel and a mint sprig.Pumpkin spice latteWinnie still thinks lotions are potions.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
